mainText:
Fonterra lifts its milk price forecast again, Samoa reaches its first Rugby League World Cup semi-final, and a six point three billion dollar crypto hack is linked to North Korea.

New Zealand.

Fonterra has raised its farmgate milk price forecast for the current season, lifting the midpoint by twenty five cents on stronger global milk powder demand. Friday's announcement follows Wednesday's rise to nine dollars seventy five, so this is a second lift in a week. It benefits dairying regions nationwide, including Waikato and the Bay of Plenty.

Fetu Samoa has beaten England to reach its first ever Rugby League World Cup semi-final. England's results on Friday leave both their men's and women's campaigns under scrutiny. The Kiwis now turn to Fiji, seeking revenge for a quarter-final loss at the twenty seventeen World Cup.

The Waitangi Tribunal says the Crown should apologise after blindsiding Māori over a decision to remove school boards' obligations to give effect to the Treaty. It found the process fell short of the standard of honour required. The finding lands in the final weekend of election campaigning.

The Electoral Commission is investigating a "Split Your Vote" website run by Harry Mowbray, who says he had no sign off from National, ACT or New Zealand First. Separately, the Commission says enrolment changes may have affected up to six thousand eight hundred people with residence class visas, after some were wrongly asked for immigration status information. An electoral law expert says there is a strong correlation between the changes and a lower enrolment rate. Election day is the seventh of November.

Auckland police have seized eighty million dollars worth of cocaine after an overseas tip off, the second large seizure in the city this week.

In Western Bay of Plenty, Dallas Hohua, convicted of manslaughter for stabbing a friend to death after a party, has had his sentence reduced and may now serve as little as two years. In Kawerau, Alan Kurtovich has confirmed his council resignation was driven by the district's Māori wards decision, the trigger for a byelection already under way.

World.

A crypto exchange, Binance, is trying to recover six point three billion US dollars stolen in a hack it calls the largest of its kind on record. Two analytics firms have attributed the attack to a North Korean hacking unit known as TraderTraitor. There is no official government confirmation of the attribution.

Wildfire and water crises continue to strain governments. Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov triggered a diplomatic rupture at the G20 in Atlanta on Friday, with European leaders refusing to be pictured alongside him, forcing organisers to cancel the traditional group photo. The United States hosted the talks as it urged members to confront threats to the economic order.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma, a safe haven city in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with residents reporting gunfire and shelling as Congolese troops were overrun. United Nations officials estimate more than one million displaced people are now inside the city.

Technology.

Google's parent company Alphabet has lost about five hundred billion US dollars in market value after revealing that its own artificial intelligence search summaries are cutting into advertising revenue. The stock hit a six month low. It follows a broader sell off in technology shares this week, with the Nasdaq opening at its lowest level in more than two months amid concern that spending on artificial intelligence, nearing one trillion US dollars, has outrun returns.

Microsoft reported soaring profits days after saying it would offer buyouts to sixty thousand workers as part of a cost cutting drive, underlining the gap between company earnings and job losses across the sector.

Sport.

Formula One. Charles Leclerc was fastest in first practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix. Liam Lawson's prospective twenty twenty seven rival, Nikola Tsolov, logged an impressive practice session in Lawson's car on his race weekend debut, before being forced out after a loss of blood in his leg. Lawson says he is trying not to overthink his future as he chases points to secure a twenty twenty seven drive. Kimi Antonelli remains on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest champion.

Rugby League World Cup. Samoa's win over England secures their first semi-final appearance in the tournament's history. The Kiwis face Fiji next, looking to avenge their twenty seventeen quarter-final exit.

Cricket. The Black Caps posted a record total against India in a Twenty20 at Eden Park, having trailed three nil in the series. Lockie Ferguson remains out with a low grade calf tear. In Cape Town, South Africa and Australia head into a decisive final day in their test series.

Netball. Silver Ferns coach Dame Noeline Taurua has dropped the mandatory Yo-Yo fitness test after seven years. Netball New Zealand has also pulled out of a proposed private league with Jenny-May Mowbray-Williams, leaving next year's competition structure unresolved.

Basketball and football. The Breakers lost one hundred and eight to one hundred and one to the Adelaide Thirty Sixers at home. Auckland FC conceded a stoppage time goal to draw one all with Brisbane Roar.

Boxing. Kiwi cruiserweight David Nyika's world title fight has been put on hold after a legal challenge from his rival forced a change of plans for his December bout. A world title fight has also opened up as an option for Joseph Parker's return to the ring.

Coming up. The Mexican Grand Prix runs this weekend, New Zealand time. The Rugby League World Cup semi-finals follow Samoa's win over England. Election day is the seventh of November.

End of flash.
